verdict.root_cause: The only positive anomaly on the board is a latency shift without errors: checkoutservice's PlaceOrder went from ~30 ms per stage early in the window to several hundred ms per stage (~650 ms total) late, every line info-level and every order succeeding [tr_c2d2f8babdf6]. cartservice keeps serving add/get/empty cart at a steady cadence with no errors, restarts or cache-connection failures [tr_9955fcf607ee] — a dependency that still answers, just slowly. Alert order (cartservice and checkoutservice at t0, frontend and loadgenerator 15s later) points at the cart leg of the checkout fan-out, and the one documented mechanism producing this shape is the repeating platform-automation cycle that attaches a traffic-shaping sidecar with fixed egress delay to the cart-service network namespace [tr_99567f16582c]. I attribute the incident to injected egress delay on cartservice making the cart call slow for checkoutservice, which waited. The change log claims the last sidecar removal landed ~1.6h before onset with nothing in the 1.3h preceding the alert [tr_99567f16582c], so either that log is incomplete near onset or a further cycle went unrecorded.
verdict.reasoning: What the system is doing wrong now is waiting — orders complete, no component errors, per-stage latency grew roughly twentyfold [tr_c2d2f8babdf6] — so the mechanism is dependency_latency, not bad_config, even though the delay is delivered as a sidecar/config edit. bad_deploy on cartservice is excluded: every image update has a matching revert (last ~1.9h before onset) and cartservice emits application logs throughout, which a non-starting image could not [tr_99567f16582c, tr_9955fcf607ee]. A lingering wrong REDIS_ADDR is excluded by its paired revert plus the total absence of cache timeout or retry errors [tr_99567f16582c, tr_9955fcf607ee]. checkoutservice is not the blamed service: no change of any kind in the 24h covering onset [tr_5854db8767ce] and no error signal of its own, only degraded timing [tr_c2d2f8babdf6]. Confidence is low because the two decisive instruments were empty — cartservice calls_total is unpopulated in both incident and baseline windows [tr_fb1f01991f7f, tr_430e028805ee], and Tempo held zero checkoutservice traces over six hours, so no child span can be timed and no sibling dependency cleared [tr_d0ff8d9d0b30]. The latency finding is itself medium-confidence from a log window whose middle ~30 minutes were truncated [tr_c2d2f8babdf6].
open_questions: Is a traffic-shaping sidecar or netem egress rule actually present in the cart-service network namespace now? The log's removal timestamp (~1.6h pre-onset) contradicts the onset timing [tr_99567f16582c], so direct inspection is required.

No trace or per-dependency latency data exists, so paymentservice, shippingservice, productcatalogservice, currencyservice and emailservice remain equally unexcluded as the slow leg [tr_d0ff8d9d0b30].

checkoutservice self-time (GC, lock contention, thread-pool queueing) is unmeasured, and the truncated middle ~30 minutes of its log window could contain errors that were never observed [tr_d0ff8d9d0b30, tr_c2d2f8babdf6].

alternatives.root_cause: A different downstream of checkoutservice (payment, shipping, product catalog, currency or email) became slow and checkoutservice waited on it.
alternatives.why_not: Empty traces neither implicate nor clear these services [tr_d0ff8d9d0b30], but none has a recorded change or any anomalous signal, whereas cartservice has a documented delay-injection mechanism and co-alerted at t0 [tr_99567f16582c].

alternatives.root_cause: checkoutservice's own in-process work (GC pauses, lock contention, thread-pool or connection-pool queueing) slowed the order path with no downstream involvement.
alternatives.why_not: Plausible only because no span breakdown or CPU/memory data exists [tr_d0ff8d9d0b30]; nothing positively supports it, and it does not explain cartservice alerting at the same instant as checkoutservice.

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed, so no effect is predicted. What this abstention asserts is that no permitted action currently has its preconditions met. revert_config on cartservice requires the evidence to name a configuration change inside the incident window; the change log names none — its last entry (the REDIS_ADDR revert) lands ~1.3h before onset and every mutation in the 26-entry cycle, including the traffic-shaping sidecar, is recorded as already reverted, the sidecar ~1.6h pre-onset [tr_99567f16582c]. Reverting to a 'prior configuration' therefore means restoring the state that the log says is already live: a no-op container recreate dressed as a fix. rollback_image is closed for the same reason on cartservice (image reverted ~1.9h pre-onset) and closed on checkoutservice by an empty change log [tr_5854db8767ce]. restart_service requires evidence pointing at process state, and cartservice logs show continuous, uninterrupted, error-free request handling with no restart or cache-connection signature [tr_9955fcf607ee]. scale_service is unavailable in this world. The next step is inspection, not mutation: confirm whether a netem/tc egress rule or traffic-shaping container is actually attached to the cart-service network namespace right now, and fix the missing checkoutservice trace export [tr_d0ff8d9d0b30] so the slow leg can be attributed at all.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if direct inspection of the cart-service network namespace finds a live traffic-shaping sidecar or netem egress delay that the change log failed to record — in which case the log is incomplete near onset, the precondition for revert_config is met by observation rather than by log, and removing that rule should drop checkoutservice PlaceOrder stage-to-stage timestamps back from several hundred ms toward the ~30 ms seen early in the window [tr_c2d2f8babdf6]. It is also wrong if per-dependency latency data, once traces are restored, shows the added time sitting in the cart call specifically rather than in paymentservice, shippingservice, productcatalogservice, currencyservice, emailservice, or checkoutservice self-time — all of which remain equally unexcluded [tr_d0ff8d9d0b30]. Note that the primary effect here is only weakly observable today: cartservice has no populated calls_total series and checkoutservice emits no traces, so confirmation would rest on hand-read log timestamp deltas alone.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is that a genuine injected egress delay persists and checkout stays at ~650 ms per order until a human inspects. That is a degradation, not an outage — orders are completing end-to-end with zero errors right up to the window close [tr_c2d2f8babdf6] — so the cost of waiting is slow carts, not lost ones. The risk of the alternative is worse: a config_revert on cartservice recreates the container on a diagnosis the change log itself contradicts, discarding in-process cache, resetting the connection for checkoutservice mid-order, and — if the slow leg is actually payment, shipping, or checkoutservice's own self-time — leaving the latency untouched while burning the one clean observation window and creating a spurious 'we changed cartservice' entry that will mislead the next responder.
proposal.blast_radius: Nobody sees a change, because none is made. Had revert_config been proposed on cartservice, the recreate would be visible to checkoutservice (direct caller on the PlaceOrder fan-out) and through it to frontend and loadgenerator, all four of which are already alerting; the cart-backing Redis would see its connections re-established. The continuing degradation this abstention tolerates is already visible to exactly that set: checkoutservice, frontend, and loadgenerator.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Four services alerted near-simultaneously along the cart/checkout/frontend path, which is not a single quiet warning and cannot be dismissed. Cartservice and checkoutservice firing together first suggests a shared downstream dependency, but the class is a weak prior.
